name: Knee raise
cue: Lift your knees to your chest with your abs, not a swing.
research: research.json biomech.knee_raise: captain's chair. Upper back pinned on the vertical back pad (thorax_back pin), shoulders depressed, upper arms vertical under the shoulders, elbows ~86 on horizontal forearm pads 0.28 H (50 cm) apart at 1.42 m (research 1.25-1.45), neutral grip on vertical handles at the pad fronts; the feet hang 24 cm clear of the base (no mounting steps: the research lists them for mounting only, and in this view a step beside a hanging heel reads as a foot rest). Hip flexion 5 -> 105 (thigh 125 deg from hanging), knee 15 -> 100, ankle -15; in the last part of the rise the pelvis curls up (posterior tilt 20: lumbar flexion 24 against the pelvis, thoracolumbar extension 4, spinal flexion 0 -> 20) while the thorax stays vertical on the pad. The lumbar segment tips top-forward, so the low back presses toward the pad as the tailbone lifts (lumbar_back gap 0.0060 -> 0.0026 H) and the hips roll up and 0.0084 H forward (hip-to-C7 chord -5.4 -> -7.3; research 0 -> -5). The return uncurls the pelvis first (via key N), then lowers the legs. Primary: rectus abdominis and the hip flexors: iliopsoas plus the proximal half of the rectus femoris (head rect_fem_up, label Hip flexors), because the iliopsoas surface proxy closes into the hip crease from the concentric through the hold and the upper rectus femoris is the hip flexor the viewer can see; the full-length rectus femoris read as a quad stripe down the thigh. Machine: a single column behind the back pad carries the pad and the arm-bar crosspiece, so no upright stands under the pelvis from the camera (two rear posts at the pad edges put the far one right under the hips, like a stool pole). Geometry: tools/design/knee_raise.mjs. Station (QA pass): two rear uprights carry the arm bars and a short spine for the back pad; side feet run forward on the floor under each arm bar and a cross member joins them at the back, so the lifter hangs between the frame sides instead of over a base plate or in front of a single post.

targets.note: trunk_flexion here is the thorax tilt (the back stays on the pad, 0 throughout); the research hip-to-C7 chord (0 -> -5) and spinal flexion (0 -> 20) are checked as trunk_chord and spinal_flexion.

camera.note: Research view az 70, el 5, turned 20 deg toward the front and raised 20 deg (az 50, el 25: 28.3 deg from the research view). Looking down over the raised knees keeps the upper rectus in view at the peak (the reduced-motion still) and the whole rectus plus the hip flexors at the stretch: phone stage glow ~1370 CSS px at the stretch and ~480 at the peak (az 60 / el 15: 1277 / 395). The station stands on two rear uprights with side feet (no plate under the lifter), so the hanging feet read as hanging between the feet of the frame, not standing on a base.
